# T*: Re-thinking Temporal Search for Long-Form Video Understanding (LV-Haystack)

> T* (TStar) is a lightweight temporal search framework for long-form video understanding that reframes costly temporal search as spatial search, introduced with the LV-Haystack benchmark in the CVPR 2025 paper "T*: Re-thinking Temporal Search for Long-Form Video Understanding" (arXiv:2504.02259) by Jinhui Ye, Zihan Wang, Haosen Sun, Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Zane Durante, Cristobal Eyzaguirre, Yonatan Bisk, Juan Carlos Niebles, Ehsan Adeli, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, and Manling Li (Stanford University, Northwestern University, Carnegie Mellon University).

What is the Long Video Haystack problem? It frames temporal search as finding a minimal set of relevant frames (for example, one to five) from tens of thousands of frames in a long video, given a specific query. What is T*? T* leverages image-based visual localization and an adaptive zooming-in mechanism that operates across both temporal and spatial dimensions, so a vision-language model (VLM) only needs to reason over a small set of retrieved keyframes.

## Key facts

- LV-Haystack is the first temporal search dataset of its kind: 480 hours of videos and 15,092 human-annotated instances for both training and evaluation.
- LV-Haystack has two subsets: HAYSTACK-EGO4D (egocentric: 988 videos, 423 hours, 15,092 QA pairs, 28,300 keyframes) and HAYSTACK-LVBENCH (allocentric: 114 videos, 26.7 hours, 342 QA pairs, 496 keyframes).
- Current state-of-the-art search methods achieve only a 2.1% temporal F1 score on the LongVideoBench subset of LV-Haystack, revealing a large research gap.
- Under a 32-frame inference budget, T* improves GPT-4o from 50.5% to 53.1% and LLaVA-OneVision-OV-72B from 56.5% to 62.4% on the LongVideoBench XL subset.
- Accepted at CVPR 2025.

## Relation to other benchmarks

Unlike long-video QA benchmarks such as LongVideoBench and Video-MME that evaluate end-to-end answer accuracy, LV-Haystack provides human-annotated reference keyframes and fine-grained metrics that disentangle temporal search quality and efficiency from downstream video question answering.
